findings.note: front : back reads the same as back : front — an axis has two ends, not a start

Nothing on the board fixes whether front-to-back should map to top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top; I picked bow→stern paralleling surface→seabed on the assumption both run 'start extreme to end extreme,' but a player could just as easily flip one half.

notes:
set-directional is inherently symmetric (bow:stern reads the same reversed) and its cross-pair order (front-back vs top-bottom) is unfixed, letting a player flip either half. Needs new pairs with an inherently ordered/asymmetric axis relationship, not a word swap within the current pairs.
- set-directional: Bow:stern and surface:seabed are each symmetric opposite-pairs (order-indistinguishable), and nothing anchors whether front-to-back should map to top-to-bottom or the reverse, so order is guessed rather than inferred.
  Try: Replace with an inherently directional relationship instead of bipolar opposites, e.g., 'source : mouth' (river start to end) paired with 'launch : voyage's end' — pick pairs where reversing the order changes the truth of the claim, not just the label.
  Or: Keep the axis idea but make each pair a graded three-plus point relationship reduced to a fixed start/end that is asymmetric by convention, e.g., 'keel : deck' (bottom-built-up structural order) paired with 'seabed : surface' only if a non-reversible convention (e.g., depth measured from surface down) is stated in the explanation and locks direction.
  Or: Drop set-directional entirely and have the pair-author supply a replacement set with a different relationship family (e.g., CASE or PART-WHOLE) that doesn't rely on a reversible spatial axis.
Do not change: set-object-component, set-representation, set-agent-object — no allowlisted finding touches them.
